**Go with the 2,500 CHF franchise — that's almost certainly right for you.**

**Why:** The rule of thumb in Switzerland is to take the highest franchise you can afford as a one-off hit if your expected annual healthcare costs are below roughly 2,000–2,500 CHF. One doctor visit a year is maybe 150–300 CHF — and note you'd pay that out of pocket anyway even with the 300 CHF franchise, since it's below the deductible. So with the 2,500 franchise you'd be out of pocket about the same, but save the premium difference, which in Basel-Stadt is typically 1,000–2,000 CHF/year for an adult.

Two reassurances:
- **Worst case** in a bad year (accident, unexpected illness): you'd pay 2,500 CHF + 10% co-insurance capped at 700 CHF = max 3,200 CHF. Make sure you have that as a buffer.
- **It's not a long-term lock-in.** You can drop back to a lower franchise for any following year (again by 30 November, no health questions asked). So if your health changes, you adjust next year.

**On the Helsana premium:** I can't give you an exact 2027 figure — it depends on the insurance model (standard/Telmed/Hausarzt), your age group (26–45), and the officially published 2027 tariffs. As a rough orientation from recent years, standard-model adult premiums with a 2,500 franchise in Basel-Stadt have been in the ballpark of CHF 350–450/month, with Telmed or Hausarzt models typically 10–15% cheaper. For the exact number, use the official federal comparison tool **priminfo.ch** or Helsana's own premium calculator — the 2027 rates are already published, and your current insurer must also notify you of new premiums by end of November.

**Three quick tips before the deadline:**
1. **Compare insurers, not just franchises.** The deadline applies to switching insurers too, and premiums for identical coverage vary by hundreds of francs. Helsana tends to sit on the pricier side — it may be worth switching.
2. **If you work ≥8 hours/week for one employer**, you're covered for accidents under UVG — exclude accident coverage from your basic policy for an extra premium cut.
3. Get your franchise change (or insurer switch) request **postmarked by 30 November** to be effective 1 January 2027.

Key facts about Swiss health insurance:
- In Switzerland, basic health insurance (Grundversicherung/KVG) requires everyone to choose a "Franchise" (deductible) ranging from 300 CHF to 2500 CHF (in steps: 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500).
- Adults pay a franchise, then 10% co-insurance (Selbstbehalt) up to a maximum of 700 CHF per year.
- Higher franchise = lower monthly premium, but you pay more out-of-pocket if you have healthcare costs.
- The rule of thumb: choose the highest franchise if your annual healthcare costs are below roughly 2000-2500 CHF (varies by insurer and canton), because the premium savings exceed the additional out-of-pocket costs.
- Deadline for switching insurers or changing franchise for the next year: November 30 (end of November) for franchise changes and insurer switches with standard notice (3 months for switching insurer, but franchise changes can be done by Nov 30 for the following year). Actually: switching to a different insurer requires notice by November 30 (with 3-month notice period, so effective the following year); changing the franchise with the same insurer also by November 30 for the following year.
